battle.name: 淮南之戰
battle.theater: 江淮濠州壽州沿淮一線
battle.brief: 顯德四年（957）春，南唐主李璟乘隙遣將攻濠州，周世宗柴榮遣趙匡胤自汴京南下，壽州、濠州攻防歷時近歲，淮南六州遂歸後周。卡面的埃及月牙劍不見於此役，它標示單刃弧身砍刀的源頭：戰場上真正的刀是唐制直刀與環首刀。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 顯德四年（957）春起，戰場鋪在長江以北、淮河南北兩岸的江淮地帶，主線是濠州（今安徽鳳陽）與壽州（今安徽壽縣）兩座淮南重鎮，東邊遠及泗州、楚州、泰州與揚州，西面則連著蔡州與汴京這條周軍的後方與漕運線。交戰一方是後周：皇帝柴榮即世宗自統大軍，樞密院掌軍政，殿前司、侍衛親軍司與殿衛司的禁軍是野戰骨幹，趙匡胤以殿前都點檢身份總領淮南方面兵馬，地方則有各道節鎮的蕃兵與州縣團練防守城邑；糧秣由汴京沿汴河轉入淮河與運道，舟船隨軍而進，人馬糧械分道而行。另一方是南唐：都金陵，以江淮精兵與舟師為依託，淮南各州分置節度使與兵將，壽州由劉仁贊屯重兵死守，楚州、揚州一線還有水軍游弋淮上，用以護糧、斷道。兩國此前已約和修好，南唐一度以侄禮稱臣、歲進方物，因此這場交兵在形式上是背盟再開，雙方都不願承認先失和局。史書多把此役記作顯德四年之淮南戰事，亦有稱壽州之役者。各家所載兵額、日期頗有出入，僅大略如此。
countriesEn: The fighting of 957 unfolded in the Jianghuai region north of the Yangtze, on both banks of the Huai River, with the main axis running through Haozhou (present-day Fengyang, Anhui) and Shouzhou (present-day Shouxian, Anhui), and reaching east to the prefectures of Si, Chu, Tai and Yang, while to the west the line joined Sui prefecture and the road up the Bian River that carried the Later Zhou's supplies back to the capital. One side was the Later Zhou: Emperor Shizong Chai Rong personally commanded the field armies, the Privy Council handled military administration, and the imperial guards of the Palace Front Office, the Imperial Guard Command and the Palace Guard formed the backbone of the field forces, with Zhao Kuangyin as commander of the Palace Front Office directing the armies in Huainan, supplemented by the troops of the regional military governors and by locally raised militia holding the cities. Grain and equipment moved from Bianjing up the Bian River and then into the Huai and the canal system, boats travelling with the army so that men, horses and supplies advanced in separate columns. The other side was the Southern Tang, based at Jinling, resting on the picked troops and the river fleet of Jianghuai, with military governors and garrisons distributed across the prefectures of Huainan; Shouzhou was held in force by Liu Renzan, while river craft patrolled the Huai around Chu and Yang both to escort grain and to cut the road. The two states had already made peace, and the Southern Tang had once styled itself a nephew of Zhou and sent annual tribute, so this campaign was in form a resumption of war after the peace had been broken, and neither camp wished to admit having broken it first. Most histories record this as the Huainan campaign of the fourth year of Xiande; it is also called the Battle of Shouzhou. The troop totals and the exact dates differ from source to source, so only the general shape can be given.
people: 後周方面的核心是皇帝柴榮。他即位未幾便在高平與北漢血戰，親冒矢石、幾為部下所棄，此後立志削平四方，淮南之役正是他推動的第一條線。趙匡胤是這場戰役最吃重的將領：時任殿前都點檢，掌內外諸軍，他自汴京率軍南下，先拔滁州，再沿淮水東進，壽州城下與南唐主力周旋多時；同年稍後的高平之戰中，正是他率侍衛死戰救出陷入重圍的世宗，使這位皇帝得以繼續南征。慕容延釗奉命西進荊南，牽制南唐西翼，兩路合擊，使李璟無法集中兵力。張永德與世宗同為郭氏姻舊，掌樞密與宿衛重地；范質、竇儀等則在朝中主張持重，范質力言北方新定、未暇遠征，竇儀進諫阻止輕進金陵，兩人雖未阻止前線取勝，卻擱下了直下江南的計劃。南唐一方，國主李璟坐鎮金陵調度，內有權臣孫晟、嚴續把持朝政，宗室之中齊王李景遂與樞密使李景達爭權不休，前線換將與籌糧屢受牽動；淮南主將劉仁贊是老將，泗州、濠州一線屢勝之後退守壽州，據城死守數月，兵敗被擒，其生死去向諸史記載不一。宋初追贈諡號之類的細節更難覈實，此處只依舊史所敘。
peopleEn: Chai Rong, the Later Zhou emperor, was the centre of gravity on the Zhou side. He had come to the throne amid the fighting at Gaoping against Northern Han, where he nearly fell and was for a moment abandoned by his own officers; the experience hardened his resolve to unify the realm, and the Huainan campaign was the first line he pushed forward. Zhao Kuangyin was the commander who carried the heaviest part of it: as commander of the Palace Front Office he held the imperial guards, led the army south from Bianjing, took Chuzhou first and then moved east along the Huai, spending months working around the Southern Tang main force at Shouzhou; in the fighting at Gaoping shortly afterwards it was again he who led the guards in a desperate charge that pulled the emperor out of a surrounded position and allowed the campaign into the south to continue. Murong Yanzhao was sent west against Nanping to pin down the Southern Tang's western flank, so that Li Jing could not concentrate his forces. Zhang Yongde, bound to the imperial house by marriage, held the Privy Council and the guard posts around the emperor, while Fan Zhi and Dou Yi argued for caution in court: Fan Zhi insisted that the north had only just been settled and was in no condition for a distant expedition, and Dou Yi counselled against a light advance on Jinling. Neither man stopped the victories on the front, but together they shelved the plan to march straight into Jiangnan. On the Southern Tang side the ruler Li Jing sat at Jinling directing the war, with powerful ministers Sun Sheng and Yan Xu holding the court, and among the imperial clan the Prince of Qi, Li Jingsui, and the military governor Li Jingda quarrelled incessantly, so that changes of commander and the gathering of grain were repeatedly disrupted; the chief commander in Huainan, Liu Renzan, was an old soldier who, after repeated successes around Si and Haozhou, withdrew to Shouzhou and held the city obstinately for several months, was captured after the city fell, and whose later fate the histories record inconsistently. Details of the posthumous titles bestowed on him under the early Song are even harder to verify, and here only the older histories are followed.
kits: 卡面上的兵器是埃及月牙劍，銅質外彎的單刃短劍，柄部收窄、刀身貼合前臂，砍擊時可以不拔刀；它比中國的直刀早了兩千多年，是人類最早的單刃劈砍刀型之一，把這件兵器放上淮南之戰的卡面，等於標示出弧身單刃、砍擊不拔這條刀劍譜系的源頭。真正在淮南戰場上出鞘的刀，則是唐制直刀與環首刀：刀身平直或微曲，單刃，柄纏皮繩或裹漆，佩於腰際；步軍用長槊、馬步軍用馬槊，遠射靠弓弩與床弩，近身格鬥仍以刀為主。護具方面，禁軍多著皮甲、札甲，披膊與護臂分列上臂與前臂，頭戴兜鍪或笠帽。南唐水軍備有舟船，沿淮河游弋，並以船隻運送糧秣與軍械。周軍攻城用拋石機、雲梯、衝車，圍城則築土城、挖壕塹，並斷敵糧道與援兵道路。軍需方面，汴京至淮上的一千餘里，靠汴河、淮河與江南運河的舟運維持，隨軍輜重車隊夾道而行，軍食一半自運，一半就地籌措。關於月牙劍本身的形制細節，各類記載有出土器與圖錄可相互印證；至於它是否真的出現在淮南則不必深究，它屬於象徵性的標記，而非本役的制式裝備。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a bronze single-edged short sword with an outward curve, a narrow hilt and a blade that lies close against the forearm, so that it cuts without having to be drawn back; it predates the Chinese straight sword by more than two millennia and is one of the earliest single-edged chopping blade types, and setting it on the card for the Huainan campaign marks the head of the lineage of the curved single edge, cut and do not withdraw. The blades actually drawn in Huainan were of another kind: the Tang-style straight sword and the ring-pommel dao, straight or slightly curved, single-edged, with the grip wrapped in hide cord or lacquer, carried at the waist; foot soldiers used the long spear and mounted troops the lance, long-range fire came from bows and crossbows, and the dao was left to close combat. For protection the imperial guards wore leather and lamellar armour, with shoulder and forearm guards, and a helmet or conical cap. The Southern Tang fleet had river craft working along the Huai, carrying grain and equipment. The Zhou besiegers used stone-throwers, siege ladders and battering rams; around the city they raised earth ramparts, dug trenches, and cut the enemy's supply road and the road of its relieving armies. On the logistics side, more than a thousand li separated Bianjing from the Huai valley, and the whole effort was sustained by boat transport on the Bian River, the Huai and the Jiangnan canal, with baggage trains moving along the road and part of the grain carried and part gathered locally. The fine details of the khopesh are documented by excavated pieces and by the old catalogues; whether it ever actually appeared in Huainan need not be pursued, for it is a symbolic marker rather than standard equipment of the campaign.
tactics: 周軍的打法是典型的中原帝國式攻勢：一路由趙匡胤領先鋒騎兵沿淮水東下，晝夜兼程插入淮南各州之間，利用南唐分兵守土、彼此不相接的弱點，逐州攻取；取得一州便置兵守城、開闢糧道，不急於深入。南唐則退守節點，以壽州、濠州為樞，倚城固守，遊騎出沒於周軍糧道側後，試圖拖慢對方推進。壽州攻城戰是全役最硬的一場：周軍不急於強攻，先在城外築土城為營，環列砲架與雲梯，外掘長壕以斷城中汲道與援兵，再以工兵日修逼近城垣；南唐守軍則以弓弩、礟石與火器拒之，屢出突襲圍營的騎兵，兩軍在城郊拉鋸逾月。同一時間，周軍另一路沿江與運道向東推進，奪取泗州、楚州、泰州、揚州，切斷南唐自江陵與金陵向淮南輸送糧兵的航道，把壽州變成孤城。配合方面，慕容延釗部攻取荊南，逼近南唐的西面屏障，使李璟無法從上游增兵。值得注意的是，進抵瓜洲之後，周軍本可乘吳越所貢的戰艦順流而下直取金陵，因朝中重臣力諫而罷兵，攻勢停在長江北岸。
tacticsEn: The Zhou method was that of a typical central plain empire on the offensive: a vanguard of cavalry under Zhao Kuangyin drove down the Huai by forced marches, inserting itself between the Southern Tang prefectures and exploiting the fact that the enemy was divided and its garrisons did not support one another; each prefecture taken was held, garrisoned and turned into a supply base, and there was no hurry to push deep. The Southern Tang in turn fell back on the strongpoints, with Shouzhou and Haozhou as the hinge, relying on the city walls, while mounted parties rode out to the flanks and rear of the Zhou supply lines in an attempt to slow the advance. The siege of Shouzhou was the hardest fight of the campaign: the Zhou did not rush the walls, but first raised earth ramparts to form a camp, ringed it with stone-throwers and siege ladders, dug long trenches to cut the city's water and its relief route, and improved the works daily with engineers until they stood close against the ramparts; the Southern Tang garrison answered with bows, crossbows, missiles and fire weapons, and repeatedly sent cavalry out to strike the besiegers' camp, and the two sides fought in the open ground outside the city for more than a month. At the same time another column of the Zhou army drove east along the river and the canal road, taking Si, Chu, Tai and Yang, and cut the waterways by which the Southern Tang fed and reinforced Huainan from Jiangling and Jinling, turning Shouzhou into an isolated city. In support, Murong Yanzhao's men took Nanping and pressed the Southern Tang's western screen, so that Li Jing could not bring up troops from the upper river. It is worth noting that when the Zhou army reached Guazhou it could have taken the ships contributed by Wuyue and run down the river straight to Jinling; the ministers persuaded the emperor to call a halt, and the offensive stopped on the north bank of the Yangtze.
data: 可核的數字有限，只能記其大概。時間上，顯德四年三月南唐先攻濠州，開啟戰端；同年秋冬季周軍進逼壽州，圍城歷時近歲，壽州於顯德五年初陷落，淮南悉平。距離上，自汴京至壽州陸路約六百餘里，汴京至瓜洲沿汴河、淮河與運道的水路則在一千餘里，遠征全靠舟船與糧車同行，淮流在壽州、濠州一段水面不寬，卻是南北漕運與軍隊過境的必爭之地。兵員方面，後周禁軍經顯德年間裁汰冗弱之後，總額約在二十萬上下，各道蕃兵與州縣團練另計；這支部隊要同時用於北拒西夏、攻取北漢與南下江淮，分兵是必然之勢。南唐江淮精兵與淮南州鎮兵的數目，各家史書只記大略，細帳已不可考。糧秣方面，圍城逾月不絕，周軍除自運漕糧，還就地徵糧、屯田，軍中以船隻屯儲、就地採買相補。傷亡方面，諸史僅記陣亡大將數人、奪取甲兵器械數萬，具體數目諸說並存，不敢妄加。器械消耗，攻城所費以砲石、柴薪與器械配件為大宗，圍城越久耗費越重，這正是壽州久攻不下、南唐主遣使議和的實力背景。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are scarce and only the general shape can be given. In time, the Southern Tang struck at Haozhou in the third month of the fourth year of Xiande and opened the war; the Zhou pushed up to Shouzhou in the autumn and winter of the same year, the siege dragging on for close to a year, and Shouzhou fell at the beginning of the fifth year of Xiande, after which all of Huainan was settled. In distance, the land road from Bianjing to Shouzhou is about six hundred li, while the water route from Bianjing to Guazhou, by the Bian River, the Huai and the canal, runs to more than a thousand li, so the expedition lived on boats and grain carts travelling together; the Huai at Shouzhou and Haozhou is not wide, yet it is the necessary passage for north-south transport and for troops on the move. In manpower, after the redundancies and weak units were cut in the Xiande years the total of the imperial guards was on the order of two hundred thousand, with the troops of the regional governors and the local militia counted apart; this force had to be used at once against Western Xia in the north, against Northern Han, and southward into Jianghuai, so splitting it was unavoidable. The figures for the Southern Tang's picked troops and for the garrison of each Huainan prefecture survive only as rough statements in the histories, the detailed returns being long lost. On supplies, a siege of many months could not be broken off: besides the grain carried up by the river, the army gathered grain locally and cultivated plots, storing grain in boats and making up the shortfall by purchase. On losses, the histories record only that a number of senior officers were killed and that tens of thousands of pieces of armour and equipment were taken, the exact figures being variously given and not to be added to on one's own authority. On the consumption of materiel, the largest items at the siege were stone shot, fuel and the fittings of the engines, and the longer the siege lasted the heavier the drain, which is the plain military background to the fact that Shouzhou did not fall quickly and that the Southern Tang ruler sent envoys to discuss peace.
cause: 淮南之戰的直接起因，落在顯德四年三月南唐主李璟主動出手。李璟本人久病，諸子與權臣爭鬥不休，淮南既是他倚以屏障江南的藩籬，又是江浙財賦輸往金陵的孔道；而北周的整軍與改革，又讓他看見南唐的守備正在空虛。於是南唐遣將自泗州、濠州一線反攻，試圖在周軍主力北上時奪回已失的州縣，把和局重新拉回自己手裡。深層的原因，是後周的國策本就是先北後南、逐步統一：柴榮在北方壓住北漢與黨項之後，必然要把矛頭指向長江以南最後一個割據政權。戰略上，吳越已與後周結盟、南平被周軍控制，南唐腹背受敵；後周則利用南唐內部傾軋、淮南守備分散的空隙，一州一州地收，避開了在江南水網中與南唐水軍正面硬拼的風險。加上世宗志在統一而非僅取一州，壽州、濠州一旦拿下，長江以北的大片土地與運河漕線就會連成一體，這才是周軍寧可冒長期圍城的風險也要拿下壽州的理由。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Huainan war was the opening move of the Southern Tang ruler Li Jing in the third month of the fourth year of Xiande. Li Jing himself had long been ill, his sons and his ministers were quarrelling without end, and Huainan was both the screen that shielded Jiangnan and the channel through which the wealth of Jiangzhe reached Jinling; the reorganising and reforming of the north meanwhile showed him that the Southern Tang's defences were being hollowed out. He therefore sent generals to strike back along the Si and Haozhou lines, trying to recover the prefectures already lost while the Zhou army was drawn north, and to pull the settlement back to his own side. The deeper cause lies in the Later Zhou's own policy of unifying the realm, first in the north and then in the south: once Chai Rong had contained Northern Han and the Tanguts in the north, the inevitable next step was the last separatist state south of the Yangtze. Strategically, Wuyue had already allied with the Later Zhou and Nanping had been taken by Zhou troops, so the Southern Tang was pressed from front and rear; the Zhou in turn exploited the internal quarrels in the Southern Tang and the scattered Huainan garrisons, taking prefecture by prefecture and avoiding the risk of a head-on clash with the Southern Tang river fleet inside the southern water network. And since the emperor's aim was unification and not merely a single prefecture, once Shouzhou and Haozhou were taken the great stretch of land north of the Yangtze and the canal road would be joined into one piece; that is why the Zhou army was willing to take the risk of a long siege at Shouzhou.
impact: 淮南入周，是後周統一事業中最關鍵的一塊拼圖。此前南北分治的界線被推到長江，此後中原王朝第一次完整控制江淮與江北，汴河、淮河以及揚州至金陵一段的漕運線可以由朝廷直接支配，江南的米財與江北的兵力從此在同一個政權調度之下；這套漕運格局在後來北宋立國之初被原樣承接，成為其財政的骨幹。南唐則被抽走最厚的一層外衣：淮南六州既失，江防只剩長江一線，南唐從此退守金陵及其周邊，國勢由盛轉衰。人事上，連年親征加重了柴榮的病勢，顯德六年正月他病逝汴京，幼主柴宗訓即位，殿前司的兵柄落在一批後周舊將手中，其中趙匡胤日後於陳橋兵變建立宋朝；為這場戰爭的勝利者，最終改寫了北宋開國的契機。戰術上，周軍止兵瓜洲、放棄直取金陵的決定，使南唐多存續了十七年，到開寶八年（975）宋軍渡江破金陵，南唐才真正亡國。兵器史上，唐制直刀與環首刀在淮南戰場上大量消耗與補製，禁軍的刀甲裝備體系在這幾年裡被重新編訂，日後北宋的軍器監製式也多有承襲。
impactEn: Huainan falling to the Zhou was the single most important piece in the Later Zhou's work of unification. The line dividing north and south was pushed back to the Yangtze, and a central plain dynasty for the first time held the whole of Jianghuai and the country north of the river; the transport line of the Bian River, the Huai and the stretch from Yangzhou to Jinling could be directed directly by the court, and the rice and wealth of the south and the soldiers of the north were for the first time managed by one government. That transport system was taken over unchanged by the early Northern Song and became the backbone of its finance. The Southern Tang, for its part, was stripped of its thickest layer: with the six prefectures of Huainan gone, nothing but the Yangtze remained as a defence, and the Southern Tang retreated to Jinling and its environs, turning from strength to weakness. In personnel terms, the campaigns of successive years worsened Chai Rong's illness; he died at Bianjing in the first month of the sixth year of Xiande, the child ruler Chai Zongxun succeeded him, and the command of the Palace Front passed into the hands of the surviving Zhou generals, among them Zhao Kuangyin, who would later establish the Song by the mutiny at Chenqiao; in that way the victor of this campaign was the man who set the terms for the opening of the Northern Song. Tactically, the decision of the Zhou army to halt at Guazhou and abandon the direct march on Jinling allowed the Southern Tang to survive a further seventeen years, until Song troops crossed the river and took Jinling in the eighth year of Kaibao (975), and the state was destroyed then. In the history of arms, Tang-style straight swords and ring-pommel dao were consumed and replaced in large numbers on the Huainan battlefield, and the system of dao and armour for the imperial guards was recompiled during those years, much of which was later carried into the Song armament works.
result: 結局是後周的全勝：濠州、壽州先後歸降，泗州、楚州、泰州、揚州隨之入周，淮南之地盡為中原所有，南唐在江淮的據點被連根拔起。壽州守將劉仁贊在城破之後被擒送京，據《舊五代史》與《資治通鑑》兩傳，其人下落或稱斬於闕下，或稱待罪不決，諸說並存；同樣記載分歧的，還有壽州城破的具體月日與南唐援軍的規模，可以確定的是南唐沒有再組織成建制的反攻。對南唐而言，淮南既失，南北界線只剩瓜洲至金陵一段，國力由攻轉守；對後周而言，此役之後再無南方割據政權的屏障，統一只剩最後一步。戰役留下的最大遺產，是那片被納入中原版圖的江淮：它餵養了後來北宋的百萬禁軍與漕運體系，也讓南唐在金陵苟延殘喘十七年，最終在開寶八年覆亡。史稱此役，或曰淮南之戰，或曰壽州之役，記載雖有詳略，方向則是一致的——中原王朝南進的第一記重拳，打在淮上。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete victory for the Later Zhou: Haozhou and Shouzhou surrendered in turn, Si, Chu, Tai and Yang followed them into Zhou hands, the whole of Huainan passed to the central plain, and the Southern Tang's footholds in the river region were torn out by the roots. After the fall of the city the commander of Shouzhou, Liu Renzan, was captured and sent to the capital; the Old History of the Five Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance give his fate either as execution below the palace or as indefinite detention, and the accounts differ. Equally divergent are the exact month and day of the city's fall and the scale of the Southern Tang relief force; what can be settled is that the Southern Tang mounted no further organized counterattack. For the Southern Tang this meant that with Huainan lost the north-south frontier was reduced to the single stretch from Guazhou to Jinling and the state's posture changed from attack to defence; for the Later Zhou it meant that after this campaign no separatist state in the south remained to screen the country, and unification was one last step away. The greatest inheritance of the war is the stretch of Jianghuai folded into the central plain's territory: it fed the million imperial guards and the transport system of the later Northern Song, and it allowed the Southern Tang to drag out a final seventeen years in Jinling before its end in the eighth year of Kaibao. The campaign is called in the histories either the Huainan war or the Battle of Shouzhou; the records vary in detail, but their direction is one and the same: the first heavy blow struck by the central plain dynasty on its march south fell on the Huai.
